body.statement: The tuple \(\theta^{\pm}\) is generated by an acyclic positive-structural-noise, positive-measurement-noise Gaussian SCM satisfying every member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) except nonnegative variance shifts, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\); its transformed second target block is \(\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0)\), so the entrywise-nonnegative ordered certificate rejects that true target.  The tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) satisfies every member condition except the common-reference restriction, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\), but its reference shift has rank one and no size-two reference principal block is positive definite.  Thus signed shifts destroy the nonnegative-diagonal necessity, while absence of a common reference destroys the rank-\(r\) carrier and the range-reconstruction step; an extension would require, respectively, baseline-variance feasibility inequalities or an aggregate carrier built from several environments.
body.justification: The result identifies exactly which parts of the certificate fail when either design restriction is removed.
body.gap: BACKSHIFT permits signed covariance changes and does not require a designated common reference, whereas the labeled principal-block fiber uses both restrictions; the explicit witnesses prevent that narrower result from being advertised as a general covariance-shift characterization.
body.consumer: Panel designers learn whether to add a lowest-variance baseline and a broad calibration environment, and analysts without them know which certificate component must be replaced rather than trusted.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\lambda^{\pm}\) and \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}\) for the two increment arrays in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\), and put \(\lambda^{w}_0=0\) for \(w\in\{\pm,\mathrm{split}\}\).  We first construct the primitive noises, so that validity of the displayed covariance tuples is not being inferred merely from their definitions.  For each \(w\), let all coordinates of \(h_e,z_e,v_e\), over \(e\in\{0,1,2\}\), be independent standard normal random variables, and define
\[
 H_e=h_e,\qquad
 \varepsilon_e=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\sqrt{\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e}\right)z_e,
 \qquad
 \eta_e=2^{-1/2}v_e.
\]
Here the square root is taken coordinatewise.  It is well defined for the signed witness because
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_1=(5/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_2=(1,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},
\]
and it is well defined for the split-reference witness because
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_1=(5/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_2=(3/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus every structural-noise covariance used in either witness is positive definite.  Set \(\Omega_{H,\mu}=I_3\).  The construction gives centered jointly Gaussian primitive vectors, mutual independence of \(H_e\), the coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\), and \(\eta_e\), the stationary latent covariance \(I_3\), and the stationary diagonal measurement covariance \(I_3/2\succ0\).  Moreover, \(B_{\mu}=0\) is acyclic, \(U_{\mu}=(I_3-B_{\mu})^{-1}=I_3\), \(C_{\mu}=0\), and every coordinate of \(\omega_{0,\mu}\) equals \(3/2>0\).  Hence, by independence and the definition of \(Y_e\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)
 =U_{\mu}\!\left(C_{\mu}\Omega_{H,\mu}C_{\mu}^{\mathsf T}
   +\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)\right)U_{\mu}^{\mathsf T}
   +\Omega_{\eta,\mu}
 =\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)+\tfrac12 I_3.
\]
This yields exactly the three covariance matrices specified for each tuple in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\).

For \(\theta^{\pm}\), the declared target set is \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\), so \(|T_{\mu}|=2=r\); every increment at coordinate \(3\) is zero; and \(\lambda^{\pm}_{11}=\lambda^{\pm}_{12}=1>0\).  Thus target cardinality, exclusion of off-target shifts, and the common-reference condition all hold.  The sole failed member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) is nonnegativity, because \(\lambda^{\pm}_{21}=-1/2<0\).  In particular, this failure does not invalidate a primitive covariance: the preceding display gives its first variance as \(3/2-1/2=1>0\).

The observable shifts of this witness are
\[
 Q=\Delta_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0),
 \qquad
 \Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0,0).
\]
For the order \(t=(1,2)\), one has \(Q_{tt}=I_2\).  To make the \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) step explicit, write
\[
 L_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\ \ell&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad D_t=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2),\qquad d_1,d_2>0.
\]
The equality \(L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T}=I_2\) gives successively \(d_1=1\), \(d_1\ell=0\), and \(d_1\ell^2+d_2=1\), hence \(L_t=I_2\) and \(D_t=I_2\).  Therefore
\[
 \Lambda_{2,t}
 =L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_2P_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0).
\]
It is diagonal but is not entrywise nonnegative.  The only other ordering is \(t'=(2,1)\).  Again \(Q_{t't'}=I_2\), the same calculation gives \(L_{t'}=D_{t'}=I_2\), and
\[
 \Lambda_{2,t'}=\operatorname{diag}(0,-1/2),
\]
which is also not entrywise nonnegative.  Consequently no ordering of the true target set satisfies \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta^{\pm},\{1,2\},t)\).  This proves, without identifying the causal target with the observable predicate, that after signed shifts are admitted the nonnegative-diagonal condition is not necessary for compatibility with the true causal target.

For \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\), the same construction verifies acyclicity, centered Gaussianity, independence, stationarity, and strict positivity of both structural and measurement noises.  Again \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\) has cardinality \(r=2\), all coordinate-\(3\) increments vanish, and every target increment is nonnegative.  Coordinate \(1\) changes in environment \(1\), while coordinate \(2\) changes in environment \(2\), so the declared target set is exactly the set of changing coordinates.  The common-reference condition alone fails, since \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_{12}=0\).

Here
\[
 Q=\Delta_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0),
 \qquad
 \Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,0).
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=1<r\).  Every size-two principal block of \(Q\) is either the zero matrix or, up to simultaneous row and column permutation, \(\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\).  Each such block has a nonzero null vector and therefore is not positive definite.  Hence no size-two candidate, including the true target \(\{1,2\}\), can pass the positive-definite reference-block requirement in \(\operatorname{Cert}\).

The failed range reconstruction is also explicit:
\[
 \operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{range}(\Delta_2)=\operatorname{span}\{(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\},
\]
so \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_2)\nsubseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\).  No procedure using only the reference range can recover the second changing direction in this witness.  By contrast, the multi-environment aggregate
\[
 \Delta_1+\Delta_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0)
\]
has rank \(2=r\) and carries both directions.  Thus an extension covering this design must replace the single-reference carrier by an object incorporating more than one environment.  Likewise, in the signed case strict validity of the primitive structural covariance requires, for each target coordinate \(j\), the inequalities
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu,j}>0,
 \qquad
 \omega_{0,\mu,j}+\lambda_{ej}>0
 \quad\text{for every }e,
\]
rather than \(\lambda_{ej}\ge0\).  These are precisely the baseline-variance feasibility inequalities exhibited by \(\theta^{\pm}\).  The two witnesses therefore establish all claimed boundary failures and the stated forms of the necessary replacements.
